description: Deterministic direct-model coding probes. Hidden validation cases live in the helper and are not included in model messages. Context size is a target; record actual model prompt token counts.
system_prompt:
You are a precise Python programmer. Complete the requested coding task.

Return only the requested complete Python function, either raw Python or one ```python code fence. No explanation, imports, decorators, annotations, helper functions, global state, I/O, or recursion. Use ordinary local variables, loops, comprehensions, indexing/slicing, arithmetic, comparisons, and basic builtins (abs, all, any, bool, dict, enumerate, int, len, list, max, min, range, reversed, set, sorted, str, sum, tuple, zip). Lambda sort keys and list append/extend/copy/sort/pop and dict get/items/keys/values are supported. Do not modify the input arguments.

cases.title: Implement normalized interval merging
cases.prompt: Implement merge_intervals(intervals). intervals is a list of pairs of integer endpoints. Normalize each pair so the smaller endpoint comes first, then merge overlapping closed intervals, including those that touch at an endpoint. Return a new list of (start, end) tuples sorted by start. Do not merge a gap: (1, 2) and (3, 4) remain separate. Duplicates and zero-width intervals are valid. An empty input returns []. For example, [(8, 5), (2, 1), (2, 6)] returns [(1, 8)]. Preserve the input.

cases.title: Repair binary search boundary behavior
cases.prompt:
Repair lower_bound(values, target). values is an ascending list of integers and may contain duplicates. Return the smallest index i such that values[i] >= target; return len(values) if no such element exists. Empty input returns 0. Use binary search (logarithmic iterations) and preserve the input. Existing buggy implementation:

```python
def lower_bound(values, target):
    left = 0
    right = len(values) - 1
    while left < right:
        middle = (left + right) // 2
        if values[middle] <= target:
            left = middle + 1
        else:
            right = middle - 1
    return left
```

Return the repaired complete function only.

cases.title: Edit a scheduler inside existing module context
cases.prompt: Update ONLY select_jobs(jobs, budget) from the module above. jobs is a list of (job_id, priority, cost) tuples with unique string IDs, integer priorities (possibly negative), and non-negative integer costs. budget is a non-negative integer. Visit jobs by descending priority, retaining original input order on equal priorities. Include a job if its cost fits the remaining budget and subtract that cost. Skip oversized jobs and continue scanning. Zero-cost jobs can still be selected after the budget reaches zero. Return a list of selected IDs in selection order. Preserve the input. This is greedy priority scheduling, not total-value maximization. Return only the complete replacement function; do not reproduce the surrounding module.
